title: Pricing by hours per project for Pressure cleaning (all heights)
audience: Owners and crew leads who quote pressure cleaning jobs and need a price that covers cost, travel, set-up, runoff control and a margin.
learningOutcomes: Calculate a cost per productive hour for a pressure cleaning round from your own figures
Estimate job hours by surface, including set-up, travel, water and runoff control, and checking time
Build a quote from hours, a rate and a margin, and state its basis, surfaces and exclusions

instruction.heading: Why hours are the starting unit for pressure cleaning
instruction.body: A pressure cleaning job is time on each surface, plus set-up, water supply, runoff control and travel. Area changes the time, and a second storey adds access time. Hours make the cost visible, so start from hours. The lead-generation guide gives a general hourly band of $40 to $100, typical $65 (What's The Damage, verified November 2026). It is an estimate, not your cost, so use it to check your hours, not to set them.

instruction.heading: Build your cost per productive hour
instruction.body: Divide the total cost of running the round by the chargeable hours in the same period. Include wages with on-costs, the vehicle, the pressure unit and its fuel or power, hoses and nozzles, detergent, insurance, phone, software and administration. Use chargeable hours only. Employee pay rates and on-costs may be set by an award or enterprise agreement; that point is unconfirmed here, so check it for each worker before using any figure.

instruction.heading: Estimate the hours by surface
instruction.body: Split each job into surfaces: driveway, path, house exterior by storey, deck or patio, and any fence. Estimate each surface in a range, using the area you measured at the site visit. Add set-up, pack-down, water connection, runoff control, travel between sites and a checking allowance. Xero's guide suggests adding 10 to 20 per cent for unexpected work (stated by the source; the BP-05 research flags whether that range is acceptable). Record actual hours after each job and the reason for any difference.

instruction.heading: Turn hours into a price
instruction.body: Multiply the total hours by the cost per productive hour to get the job cost. Divide by one minus your target margin to get the price. Apply the materials policy and the minimum charge. Show the storey and the runoff control as named lines. The lead-generation guide gives no percentage for storeys and no minimum charge, so the storey and minimum lines must come from your own records.

instruction.heading: Check the price against the market, without copying it
instruction.body: The lead-generation guide's typical prices for a driveway ($250) and a concrete path ($140) add to $390. A quote below that sum is not automatically wrong, because surface, access and area differ. It is a prompt to check your hours for each surface, and to explain the difference. Do not use the typical figures as a target.

instruction.heading: Keep the quote honest
instruction.body: A pressure quote states the surfaces and their measured areas, the storey, the hours or price basis, the exclusions, what the client must provide (water, access and clear vehicles), and how long the quote is valid. Quotes without a site visit are estimates, so say so. Re-quote when the surfaces change.

procedure: Gather the year's total round costs and the chargeable hours achieved in the same period.
Divide total costs by chargeable hours to get the cost per productive hour.
Measure each surface at the site visit, then estimate the time for each as a range.
Add set-up, water connection, runoff control, travel and checking time as named lines.
Multiply total hours by the cost per productive hour, then divide by one minus the margin.
Apply the materials policy and the minimum charge.
Write the quote with surfaces and areas, hours basis, exclusions, client inputs and validity.
Record actual hours after each job and compare them with the estimate.

workedExamples.situation: Illustrative figures only, not market rates. A driveway of about 40 square metres and a front path, both measured at the site visit. The owner estimates 1.5 hours on the driveway, 1 hour on the path, 0.5 hours of travel and 0.5 hours of set-up and runoff control, a total of 3.5 hours. The owner's cost per productive hour is $60 AUD (illustrative). The target margin on price is 25 per cent (illustrative).
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the job cost, what is the price with a 25 per cent margin on price, and how should the result be checked against the lead-generation prices?
workedExamples.reasoning: The cost is 3.5 hours multiplied by $60 AUD, which is $210 AUD. The price is $210 divided by 0.75, which is $280 AUD. The lead-generation typicals for a driveway ($250) and a concrete path ($140) add to $390, so the quote is below that sum. The owner checks the hours for each surface and the set-up and runoff time before deciding whether the difference is right. The typicals show where the market sits; they do not set the price.

equipmentAndPpe: Quote worksheet or spreadsheet with a line for each surface
Time log for each job, with estimated and actual columns
Measuring tape or laser measure for surface areas
PPE as listed in {{business:safety.required_ppe}}, and the access method for any storey

commonErrors.error: Pricing from the hourly wage alone
commonErrors.prevention: Include on-costs, vehicle, pressure unit, consumables, insurance and administration in the cost per productive hour.

commonErrors.error: Counting paid hours as productive hours
commonErrors.prevention: Use chargeable hours only when calculating the cost per productive hour.

commonErrors.error: Leaving out set-up, water and runoff control time
commonErrors.prevention: Add these as named lines on every estimate.

commonErrors.error: Quoting with no exclusions for panels, roofs or water supply
commonErrors.prevention: List what is excluded, what the client provides and the access assumptions.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Pricing guidance only. The ACCC says misleading price statements are prohibited. State and territory fair trading rules also apply.

Runoff time is part of the hours. The EPA Victoria car-repair sheet does not cover washing outdoor surfaces, so check the runoff rule for driveway and house washing with EPA Victoria before you price the containment line.
Victoria: the working-at-height rule for storeys and ladders was not checked in this draft. Check the Victorian rule with WorkSafe Victoria before allowing time for any storey.
Award, enterprise agreement and on-cost rates for employees are unconfirmed in this research. Check which instrument applies to each worker.

qualityStandard: Each quote shows surfaces and measured areas, hours or price basis, exclusions, client inputs and validity.
The cost per productive hour is calculated from the owner's own records and dated.
Actual hours are recorded for at least the first ten pressure jobs of each surface type and compared with the estimate.
documentationEvidence: Cost per productive hour worksheet, dated, with the source of each figure
Quote showing surfaces, areas, hours basis, exclusions and validity
Job time log with estimated and actual hours by surface
summary: A pressure cleaning job is time on each surface, so start every quote from hours.
Cost per productive hour uses chargeable time, not paid time.
Set-up, runoff control, travel and checking time are named lines, not hidden extras.
Compare estimates with actual hours, and change the method when they diverge.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which costs belong in the cost per productive hour for a pressure cleaning round?
options: Only the hourly wage of the lowest-paid worker and nothing else from the accounts or the rent
The price the client pays, plus the deposit, the late fee and the crew bonus paid
The average hourly rate of competitors in the local area and their fees for the whole year
Wages with on-costs, vehicle, pressure unit, consumables, insurance and administration, divided by chargeable hours

knowledgeChecks.question: A driveway and path job is estimated at 3.5 hours and takes 5. What is the right response?
options: Record the actual hours, find the cause, and adjust the estimate and future quotes
Leave the estimate, since the client has already paid and the crew has finished
Reduce paid hours for the crew on the next job and skip the morning break
Raise the price for this client's next job only and no one else is charged more

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does a pressure cleaning quote need an exclusions list?
options: To hide the margin from the client and to keep the rates a secret from the crew
To make the quote longer and to fill up the page with more text and words for the client
To show what the price covers, so scope changes can be priced and disputes are reduced
To lower the client's expectations and to make the job seem much smaller than it is

sourceReferences: What's The Damage, 'Pressure washing cost guide', https://whatsthedamage.com.au/pressure-washing-cost/, verified November 2026, metadata 2026-11-01. Lead-generation estimates; used as a sense-check only.

business.gov.au, 'Choose a pricing strategy', https://business.gov.au/products-and-services/choose-a-pricing-strategy, page metadata dated 1 October 2026. Supports: on-costs such as leave and superannuation belong in the hourly cost.
ACCC, 'Setting prices: what's allowed', https://www.accc.gov.au/business/pricing/setting-prices-whats-allowed, last modified 15 July 2026. Supports: misleading price statements are prohibited.

Xero Australia, 'How to price services', https://www.xero.com/au/guides/how-to-price-services/, dated 3 September 2026. Supports: divide by billable hours; add a set allowance for delays; figure stated by source of 10 to 20 per cent for unexpected work.

EPA Victoria, 'Stormwater management for car repair industry', publication 1333.1, March 2015, https://www.epa.vic.gov.au/-/media/epa/files/publications/1333-1.pdf. Car-repair sheet; does not cover outdoor surfaces.

Carters Trade Leader, 'Estimating how many hours a job will take', https://tradeleader.carters.co.nz/trade-skills/estimating-how-many-hours-a-job-will-take-why-83-get-it-wrong/, dated 1 October 2025. New Zealand publisher; general method only.

Work Health and Safety (Managing the Risk of Falls at Workplaces) Code of Practice 2015, https://legislation.gov.au/F2016L00425/asmade/2016-03-30/text/original/epub/OEBPS/document_1/document_1.html, registered 2016. Commonwealth code; not Victorian law. Cited for the height point; the Victorian rule was not checked.

WorkSafe Victoria, news release on falls risks in the solar sector, https://www.worksafe.vic.gov.au/news/2026-08/crackdown-falls-risks-solar-sector, 26 August 2026. Supports: allowing workers onto a roof without adequate protection is unlawful, even with no incident. Aimed at solar; the principle is stated for any roof.
Note: award, enterprise agreement and on-cost rules, and state fair trading rules, are UNCONFIRMED for pressure cleaning. No per-square-metre price or pressure-cleaning hours benchmark was found.
